{{short description|Dutch-American mathematician}}
'''Hans Gerard Kaper''' (born June 10, 1936)<ref name="ug"/> is a Dutch-American mathematician who worked for many years at [[Argonne National Laboratory]] until his retirement in 2008. He continues to hold adjunct professorships in mathematics and statistics at [[Georgetown University]] and in music at the [[University of Illinois at Urbana–Champaign]],<ref name="home">[http://www.mcs.anl.gov/~kaper/ Home page], [[Argonne National Laboratory]], retrieved 2015-02-08.</ref> where he has been a long-term collaborator on the UIUC Computer Music Project.<ref>[http://ems.music.uiuc.edu/cmp/history CMP History] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150209084214/http://ems.music.uiuc.edu/cmp/history |date=2015-02-09 }}, School of Music, UIUC, retrieved 2015-02-08.</ref>

Kaper was born in [[Alkmaar]], [[Netherlands]],<ref name="ug">[http://hoogleraren.ub.rug.nl/?page=showPerson&type=hoogleraar&hoogleraar_id=1331&lang=en Faculty profile], [[University of Groningen]], retrieved 2015-02-08.</ref> and earned a PhD in 1965 from the [[University of Groningen]] under the supervision of Adriaan Isak van de Vooren.<ref>{{mathgenealogy|id=117044}}</ref>
He taught briefly at Groningen before joining Argonne.<ref name="ug"/>
At Argonne, he directed the Mathematics and Computer Science Division.<ref name="asli"/> He is also the editor-in-chief of ''SIAM News'', the newsletter of the [[Society for Industrial and Applied Mathematics]] (SIAM).<ref>[http://sinews.siam.org/about-siam-news.aspx About ''SIAM News''], retrieved 2015-02-08.</ref> In 1989 he became correspondent of the [[Royal Netherlands Academy of Arts and Sciences]].<ref>{{cite web |author= |url=https://www.knaw.nl/en/members/correspondents/4339 |title=Hans Kaper |publisher=Royal Netherlands Academy of Arts and Sciences |date= |accessdate=18 July 2015 |archive-date=21 July 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150721211041/https://www.knaw.nl/en/members/correspondents/4339 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

Since retiring, Kaper has investigated the mathematics of [[climate change]], and directs the [[National Science Foundation|NSF]]-funded Mathematics and Climate Research Network.<ref name="home"/>
With Hans Engler of Georgetown, he is a co-author of the book ''Mathematics and Climate'' (SIAM, 2013),<ref>{{citation|title=Review of ''Mathematics and Climate'' by H. Kaper and H. Engler|first=Steve|last=Schecter|journal=Dynamical Systems Magazine|date=July 2014|url=http://www.dynamicalsystems.org/ma/ma/display?item=516}}.</ref><ref>{{citation|title=Hans Kaper and Hans Engler: ''Mathematics and Climate'' and Ian Roulstone and John Norbury: ''Invisible in the Storm: The Role of Mathematics in Understanding Weather''|first=Sebastian|last=Reich|journal=Jahresbericht der Deutschen Mathematiker-Vereinigung|date=September 2014|volume=116|issue=3|pages=183–185|doi=10.1365/s13291-014-0092-8|s2cid=115948662}}.</ref><ref>Review of ''Mathematics and Climate'' by John Adam, {{MR|3137118}}</ref><ref>[http://www.maa.org/publications/maa-reviews/mathematics-and-climate Review of ''Mathematics and Climate''] by William J. Satzer (December 2013), MAA Reviews, [[Mathematical Association of America]].</ref> which won the 2013 ASLI Choice Award of the Atmospheric Science Librarians International.<ref name="asli">[http://www.mcs.anl.gov/articles/new-textbook-wins-2013-choice-award New textbook wins 2013 Choice Award], [[Argonne National Laboratory]], March 11, 2014, retrieved 2015-02-08.</ref>

In 2009, Kaper and his son [[Tasso J. Kaper]] (a mathematician at [[Boston University]]) were simultaneously honored as [[fellow]]s of SIAM.<ref>[http://www.anl.gov/articles/three-argonne-mathematicians-recognized-siam-fellows Three Argonne mathematicians recognized as SIAM Fellows] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150209072820/http://www.anl.gov/articles/three-argonne-mathematicians-recognized-siam-fellows |date=2015-02-09 }}, [[Argonne National Laboratory]], retrieved 2015-02-08.</ref>
